::: {.session-strip}
[10 min, before the session]{.chip} [Python 3.10 to 3.12 · Julia · Dynawo 1.7.0]{.chip}
:::

The notebooks need three things next to Python. **pypowsybl** comes from pip. **Julia with PowerModels.jl** solves the optimal power flow inside GridFM-Datakit and installs itself on first use. **Dynawo** is a native simulator distributed as a zip archive. Pick the route that suits your machine.

| Route | Works on | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| [GitHub Codespaces](#codespaces) | Any browser | One click, a few minutes to build |
| [Dev container](#container) | Any OS with Docker | One command |
| [Local install](#local) | Linux, Windows through WSL 2 | About ten minutes |

::: {.callout-note title="macOS"}
Dynawo ships Linux and Windows builds only. On a Mac, use Codespaces or the dev container.
:::

## GitHub Codespaces {#codespaces}

Open the repository in a codespace. The dev container installs Python, Julia, PowerModels and Dynawo, then opens the notebooks.

[Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/gfm6w/tutorial?quickstart=1){.btn .btn-primary}

The first build takes several minutes. Start it before the session.

## Dev container {#container}

With Docker and VS Code, clone the repository and choose **Reopen in Container**. Without VS Code, build and run the image directly.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gfm6w/tutorial.git
cd tutorial
docker build -t gfm6w-tutorial -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile .
docker run --rm -p 8888:8888 -v "$PWD":/workspace gfm6w-tutorial
```

Then open the link printed by Jupyter.

## Local install {#local}

### 1. Python packages

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gfm6w/tutorial.git
cd tutorial
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

The requirements pin GridFM-Datakit to the `gfm6wt` branch, which carries the dynamic event randomization and the PowSyBl reader fixes used here.

### 2. Julia and PowerModels

```bash
gridfm_datakit setup_pm
```

This downloads Julia if needed, then PowerModels.jl and Ipopt. Count a few minutes.

### 3. Dynawo

```bash
bash scripts/install_dynawo.sh
```

The script downloads Dynawo 1.7.0 into `~/dynawo` and declares it to PowSyBl in `~/.itools/config.yml`. To use an existing installation, write that file yourself.

```yaml
dynawo:
  homeDir: /path/to/dynawo
  debug: false
```

### 4. Check

```bash
python scripts/check_setup.py
jupyter lab notebooks/
```

`check_setup.py` prints the versions found and runs a ten-second Dynawo simulation. If it ends with `All set`, you are ready.

## Follow along without installing

Every page of this site was executed end to end, so all outputs are visible. You can read along and run the notebooks later.
